taste.name: Landscape Is the Interface
taste.trigger: When placing navigation, cards, and CTAs on top of continuous full-bleed Antarctic photography and video
taste.decision: Chose translucent glass surfaces (rgba(0,0,0,0.1-0.2) pills, white translucent panels, 2-layer white inset hairlines) over opaque white cards, drop shadows, or letterboxing imagery in a contained column
taste.reason: A visitor deciding on a six-figure expedition is buying the place, not the website; every opaque pixel of UI is a pixel of Antarctica they cannot see, so the interface must behave like a window annotation, not a document
evidence: translucent black backgrounds cover 21.2% of bg area

taste.name: Type as Territory Marker
taste.trigger: When making a scrolling page about vast empty terrain feel vast rather than like a brochure
taste.decision: Chose a jump scale with ~3x leaps (14px UI, 42px serif headings, then 140/256/320px condensed wordmarks) over a conventional 1.25x modular ratio that would fill the 50-130px middle band
taste.reason: Monument-scale type that overflows the viewport makes the reader feel physically small relative to the word, mimicking standing before the landscape; mid-size headlines would read as marketing, not geography
evidence: sizeDistribution: 14px x72, 42px x14, 140px x1, 256px x1, 320px x1

taste.name: One Orange Pin
taste.trigger: When they could have deployed a brand accent across CTAs, links, icons, and hovers as luxury-travel competitors do with gold or brand hues
taste.decision: Chose to let photography carry 100% of the chroma and restricted saturated color to a single element, the fixed #FF7E15 'How it works' tab; even the two primary CTAs (Rates, Enquire) are colorless glass
taste.reason: Expedition gear logic: in a white-and-ice world, one orange marker is instantly findable precisely because nothing else competes; a second orange element would halve the first one's power

taste.name: Slow-Ease Traversal
taste.trigger: When deciding how a 20782px, 14-viewport-deep narrative page should feel to move through
taste.decision: Chose long heavy easing (0.45s cubic-bezier(0.76,0,0.24,1), transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1)) over snappy 150-200ms ease-out microinteractions, and accepted shipping without prefers-reduced-motion or :focus-visible support
taste.reason: Sub-200ms motion says efficient tool; 450-600ms motion with symmetric-power easing says heavy things moving through cold air — the pacing itself communicates expedition gravity, a deliberate bet of cinematic mood over accessibility hedging
